restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes: 2^96 uniform prefixes m0..m14 and every m15 in each group.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256, prefix rounds 0 and 1, one root block, flags 11, length 64, counter 0.
Four consecutive t-values are evaluated together by packing four 32-bit lanes into each 256-bit word.
A 160-bit Briggs-Torczon sparse set stores the first occupant of each key. Full 256-bit equality is rechecked with two target compressions.
Verification attempts are capped at 2^110. The run aborts after that cap.
Word primitives are charged at 192 per message, above a listed 108.5, with C=430.
Success probability 0.39 is conditional on heuristic H1. The time cap is not.
baseline_improved names the nominal reference only and does not assert that a promoted qualified attack was improved.

heuristics.statement: For events F1, F2, and Fcap, the 2^128 digests of the grouped messages may be treated as mutually independent and uniform on 256-bit strings.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability of this message family. Not used to justify the time cap, lane packing, or the final rehash.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 20-bit projections of 2^10-message grouped samples to independence of the full 256-bit digests at 2^128 messages.
heuristics.limitations: Shared prefixes make independence unproved. The experiments are small masked projections with public seeds, not a full-scale trial and not a confidence interval. The claim keeps the model probability above 0.393 and submits 0.39.
